newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. spot resids steady to firmer with crude.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. spot resids steady to firmer with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices, buoyed by another sharp rally in crude, were steady to firmer again Monday, but trade remained light, with many out for the Columbus Day holiday or attending an industry conference.

"I don't think anything got done today. Everyone was out (for the holiday) or in Williamsburgh (Virginia). But I just don't see resid going down with crude back up and bunkers still strong," said one cash trader.
In New York Harbor, firm bunkers again boosted talk for high sulphur grades, with 2.2 percent up a quarter to near the $20 a barrel mark, traders said.
NYH three percent was up a similar amount to the $19.50-75 area, while one percent again held steady at about $21.25.
The complex continued to defy some predictions for lower prices in the face of slack utility fuel burns from cheap natgas and relatively mild weather.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent still at $20.00-25 and three percent in the mid-$20 area.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
Gas at the New York City gate slipped almost five cents Monday to the mid-$2.60s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.37/mmBtu equivalent.
